<!--

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
The `yeelight` integration now uses custom SSDP-like discovery instead of the mDNS discovery since mDNS discovery is removed in new firmwares (#26574). After this change, there will be no longer automatic configuration based on the `discovery` integration. Users currently using that should set up all devices through UI.

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
It seems that adding config flow to yeelight is the best way to support the custom SSDP-like discovery. This PR added config flow to the yeelight integration.

## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!

Hey there @rytilahti, @zewelor, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`yeelight`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L476) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Now users can configure discovered devices through option flow by first pick up a device. Not sure if this is the best way to do. Maybe add buttons to the device page like ZHA and MQTT that is newly introduced in 0.112 is better, but that will require frontend works.
I just tried this PR via a custom_component folder and it works really well! Thank you!
Almost done. Mark as ready for review.

Great job !

Regarding parts around yeelight device, it looks good to me. I don't have any experience with config flow, so cannot really review that part. Didn't tested it, I will be able to do it in next week.

I tested this PR in my development environment and the configuration flow works very well. But there is a problem with updating lights state by HA. When I turn the light on/off, it takes 5-15 seconds to register this change by HA. The physical light turns on/off immediately.
It looks like this:

![yeelight](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/478555/87028805-73081a00-c1df-11ea-8a41-e53806c83eeb.gif)
@bieniu Yeah I noticed that as well. Turns out I forgot to update the states after turning on/off. I'll fix it soon.
@bieniu It is now fixed.

Too much is going on in this PR. We're adding:
- New tests for platforms
- Update coordinator
- Config flow

Please break it up in at least three different PRs in the above order. We're also changing to use async api in some places. That could be a fourth PR if not tightly coupled to one of the above.

@MartinHjelmare Thanks for the advice. The tests for platforms currently rely on config entries so I'll probably add them when the config flow is merged. I'll first move functions to async to make things easier, then add update coordinator. Then maybe some refactors to prepare for config flow.

I made some changes to this PR. `DataUpdateCoordinator` is now changed back to the original `track_time_interval` implementation. Most async functions are changed back to sync versions. As long as the platform test PR (#37745) is merged, this one should be good to go.

@shenxn As already mentioned I tried this PR (prior the split into different PRs) and noticed the following.
Depending on the way of setup (manual vs discovery) the actual devices are listed differently:
![Screenshot_2020 07 14_14h16m21s_015_](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1368405/87424914-1e004580-c5dd-11ea-9425-d886b36debaf.png)
![Screenshot_2020 07 14_14h16m50s_016_](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1368405/87424918-1f317280-c5dd-11ea-8cce-ba1ca9592a91.png)

On my one installation, the lights are just listed as devices and on the other the devices are listed directly in the integration card. Where does this difference come from and is it intended? 

Just wanted to notify you about this so you can (maybe) fix it during the refactoring.

@TheZoker Yes, this is expected. Since when you set up discovery, there is only one config entry. However, when set up manually, you'll need one config entry for each device. In previous versions of HA, different config entries are shown in different cards. Now different config entries of the same integration are combined into one single card.
@shenxn Any news on this PR? 🙂
@TheZoker The platform tests (#37745) should be able to be merged shortly. Then after some rebase work, this PR will be ready for review.

@mikeage We'll be using a customized discovery protocol and we don't use zeroconf. So I think this is not going to be a problem.
Ok. My concern was whether zeroconf would still detect it, even if not asked (note that it's not advertising as `_miio._udp` which is what Yeelights use now, and yet it's still found).

If your yeelight device responses to the standard SSDP discovery, then zeroconf is going to detect it. Even if it gives a valid name, as long as the suffix is not registered in the manifest, zeroconf will just ignore that.

ok, thanks. It seems like because the 2.x series of FW now supports homekit, this is a legitimate issue. It is ignored because of the `try`/`except`, but it does leave a bunch of scary looking messages in the log. I think #38914 should cover it.

I think this is a bug in the yeelight firmware that gives invalid SSDP name. If you don't want that scary looking message, maybe the log level should be changed from `exception` to `warning` in `zeroconf`.

Please rebase and update to latest black version. We bumped version a couple of days ago.

After the 0.106.5 update all my Yeelight color2 has been dissapeared. I was using the auto mode. Now with manual mode it is working again. But I would like to back to the auto mode.

## Environment

- Home Assistant release with the issue:  0.106.5

- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Home Assistant (current name)
- Integration causing this issue: not sure about that discovery or yeelight
- Link to integration documentation on our website:  https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/discovery/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->
Not working config:
```yaml
discovery:
  ignore:
    - igd
```

Working config:
```yaml
discovery:
  ignore:
    - igd
    - homekit
    - yeelight

yeelight.yaml
devices:
  192.168.1.y:
    name: 'XXX'
  192.168.1.y:
    name: 'YYY'
```

## Traceback/Error logs

```txt
There is no lines about that problem
```

I see everytime a notification about HomeKit not present in previous versions.
comments: Hey there @rytilahti, @zewelor, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`yeelight`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L417) for? Thanks!
I can replicate it in another hardware (the production one). Restoring to Home Assistant 0.106.3 it is enought for the Yeelight to start working again.
Same problem with my new HA installation (Raspberry), manual config works but I can't set fixed IPs (ISP wants DHCP disabled) (and Yeelight fw doesn't support static IP config)

Same issue with a CT light. With my color bulbs or color strips, I have not issue.
:-/

FYI I still have this issue with "Home Assistant 0.108.6" and I also have a weird notification to add Yeelight Strips to "HomeKit".

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12491721/79687364-0d8f3780-8247-11ea-8ebf-ceb857209c97.png)

Edit:  Went back to 0.100.1 and didn't work too .. :/

This issue is still present

Problem:
The bulb is auto-discovered as HomeKit device, but then I don't have a [HomeKit pin](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homekit_controller) to pair it... This is not usable. The bulb should be auto-discovered directly, and if necessary show config option to choose version (white light, temperature light, color, strip...).

Only way to make it to work is by putting manual entry in config.yaml
If you have anything better than basic white lamp, you also need to go through docs to find correct model name string

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3856578/81290262-ad2e3180-905f-11ea-886d-27f3ae17b9a3.png)

I'm also having this issue as described by @Zireael 

@zewelor @rytilahti Will this get fixed by https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/35448 ?
That linked PR will allow automatic detection of the model, so that part of the problem will be fixed. Autodiscovering existing bulbs will require another PR.

> That linked PR will allow automatic detection of the model, so that part of the problem will be fixed. Autodiscovering existing bulbs will require another PR.

Thanks for the quick reply. Do you have any suggestions how we can move the autodiscovery forward?

The integration needs to be converted to use a config flow to do the detection. One of the blockers for that was the lack of an unique id, so that PR by @zewelor will allow proceeding to do that conversion.
